summary.en: The Indigenous Guard has taken up arms against President De la Espriella after a fifth bombing killed nine ELN members and a separate army bombing killed eight ELN fighters in the southwest. A car bomb at Casanare toll booths injured four women, while a drone strike in Guapi, Cauca killed one Marine and wounded four soldiers. Ten ELN fighters were killed in a strike in Cauca, and ten rebels from the ELN were killed in a separate incident. Viviane Morales has been reappointed to De la Espriella’s government and Mocho Olmedo, head of Front 33, was extradited to the United States. 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den urfolksgarden har tatt opp våpen mot president De la Espriella etter at et femte bombeangrep drepte ni ELN-medlemmer og et separat hærangrep drepte åtte ELN-krigere i sørvest. En bilbombe ved bomstasjonene i Casanare såret fire kvinner, mens et droneangrep i Guapi, Cauca drepte en marine og såret fire soldater. Ti ELN-krigere ble drept i et angrep i Cauca, og ti rebeller fra ELN ble drept i en separat hendelse. Viviane Morales er gjenutnevnt til De la Esprielleas regjering og Mocho Olmedo, leder for Front 33, ble utlevert til USA. 225 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
